overallAssessment.verdict: data/regions/south-wales.ts contains a usable structural skeleton but is notably thin compared to other region files — only 5 topExperiences (vs 12 for Pembrokeshire) and 3 FAQs. No source citations are recorded anywhere in the file (the comment header lists no provenance at all). All specific claims — including the Bike Park Wales day-pass price, transport frequencies, canal towpath length, and Cwmcarn trail status — must be treated as unverified. Three issues require human decision before publishing: (1) the hero image has no provenance; (2) there is no OG/social image at all — the meta object entirely lacks a socialImage field and no south-wales-og.jpg exists on disk; (3) the '30 minutes from Cardiff' travel-time claim for Merthyr Tydfil appears overstated and needs correction. Additionally the page focuses narrowly on the valleys/industrial heritage framing rather than the full 'South Wales' geographic scope, which may create SEO mismatch for users expecting coastal, Vale of Glamorgan, or Newport/Monmouthshire content.
overallAssessment.structuralQuality: LOW-MEDIUM — correct TypeScript shape and all required top-level keys are present but content is sparse. topExperiences has only 5 entries, FAQs only 3, hiddenGems only 2, localEatsAndDrinks only 2. No operator slugs, no schema markup data, no seasonal images.
overallAssessment.factualConfidence: LOW-MEDIUM — core geographic facts (valley names, Big Pit free entry, canal existence, Brecon Beacons access) are stable. All pricing, transport frequency details, and the Cwmcarn Forest operational status need human verification before publishing.

criticalIssues.issue: '30 minutes from Cardiff' travel claim for Merthyr Tydfil/Brecon Beacons appears overstated
criticalIssues.location: data/regions/south-wales.ts — keyFacts[3]: { label: 'Distance from Cardiff', value: '30 minutes', detail: 'Merthyr Tydfil or Brecon Beacons access' }
criticalIssues.diagnosis: Transport for Wales valley line trains from Cardiff Central to Merthyr Tydfil take approximately 55-65 minutes (not 30 minutes). By car on the A470, the journey is approximately 40-55 minutes depending on traffic. The Storey Arms car park (Pen y Fan trailhead, A470) is approximately 45-55 minutes by car. '30 minutes' is materially inaccurate and will cause visitor frustration. The FAQ correctly says 'Valley Lines trains from Cardiff run every 15-30 minutes to Merthyr' (frequency, not journey time) — the keyFact appears to have confused frequency with journey time.
criticalIssues.action: HUMAN EDITORIAL DECISION: correct to accurate travel time. Suggested: '55-65 min by train, 45-55 min by car' or simply '1 hour'. Verify current TfW journey time at https://www.tfwrail.wales/.

verified_or_stable.claim: Main Valleys: Rhondda, Cynon, Taff, Rhymney — former coal heartland
verified_or_stable.note: These are the four principal valleys of the South Wales coalfield. Geographically stable, well-documented. The Rhondda, Cynon, and Taff valleys converge near Pontypridd. The Rhymney Valley runs through Caerphilly borough.

verified_or_stable.claim: Big Pit National Coal Museum — free entry, underground tour
verified_or_stable.note: Big Pit (Pwll Mawr) is part of the National Museum Wales (Amgueddfa Cymru) network. Like all Amgueddfa Cymru sites, general admission is free. Underground tours are included in the free ticket. The mine is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (as part of the Blaenavon Industrial Landscape). Booking ahead is strongly recommended. Located in Blaenavon, Torfaen.

verified_or_stable.claim: Big Pit — part of Blaenavon UNESCO World Heritage Site
verified_or_stable.note: The Blaenavon Industrial Landscape was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2000. Big Pit and Blaenavon Ironworks are the core elements. Well-documented.

verified_or_stable.claim: Bike Park Wales — UK's first full-scale mountain bike park, located near Merthyr Tydfil
verified_or_stable.note: Bike Park Wales (BPW) opened in 2013 at Gethin Woodland in Cwmtaf, above Merthyr Tydfil, and is widely recognised as the first full-scale, uplift-served mountain bike park in the UK. Real operator with a live booking website.

verified_or_stable.claim: Monmouthshire and Brecon Canal — towpath walking and cycling
verified_or_stable.note: The Monmouthshire and Brecon Canal is a real canal that runs through the Brecon Beacons National Park and into south-east Wales. The towpath is a well-used walking and cycling route. The navigable section from Brecon to Pontymoile (near Pontypool) is approximately 35 miles (56km). Canal and River Trust manages the waterway.

verified_or_stable.claim: Rhondda Heritage Park — mining history site
verified_or_stable.note: Rhondda Heritage Park is a real visitor attraction at the former Lewis Merthyr Colliery in Trehafod, Rhondda Cynon Taf. It offers underground tours, exhibitions, and family activities. Admission is charged (not free). Note: the TS data does not explicitly claim it is free, only that it 'tells the valley story'. Verify current admission pricing before publishing.

verified_or_stable.claim: Dare Valley Country Park near Aberdare
verified_or_stable.note: Dare Valley Country Park is a real country park on a former colliery site near Aberdare, managed by Rhondda Cynon Taf County Borough Council. Free access to the park itself. Visitor centre on site.

The Clydach Gorge (Cwm Clydach) is a real Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and Local Nature Reserve in Blaenau Gwent/Monmouthshire, running from Brynmawr to Abergavenny. It contains industrial archaeology (old railway, ironworks remains) and woodland. Access is managed by NRW and local authorities.

Pontsticill Reservoir is a real reservoir in the Brecon Beacons National Park, approximately 5 miles north of Merthyr Tydfil. It is managed by Dŵr Cymru Welsh Water. Walking access is possible from the reservoir road. The TS data lists it as a 'wild swimming' hidden gem — wild swimming at reservoirs in Wales is technically on private water utility land and may be discouraged. This should be reviewed.

verified_or_stable.claim: Bunch of Grapes, Pontypridd — craft beer pub
verified_or_stable.note: The Bunch of Grapes is a real pub/restaurant in Pontypridd, well-regarded for craft beer and food. Real operator.

verified_or_stable.claim: Waterfall Country — Sgwd yr Eira and Four Falls area accessible from south Wales valleys
verified_or_stable.note: Waterfall Country (Waterfall Woods/Ystradfellte area) is in the Brecon Beacons National Park near Pontneddfechan, approximately 30-35 miles from Cardiff and accessible via Merthyr Tydfil or Hirwaun. Sgwd yr Eira (where you can walk behind the waterfall) and the Four Falls Trail are real, well-documented NRW managed walks. The claim that this is accessible from the 'southern valleys' is directionally correct though the waterfalls are technically in Neath Port Talbot/Powys. The NRW car park at Pontneddfechan is the standard access point.
De Cymru is the correct Welsh-language name for South Wales.

verified_or_stable.claim: South Wales Metro — valley lines from Cardiff transport programme
verified_or_stable.note: The South Wales Metro is a real, ongoing Transport for Wales infrastructure programme upgrading valley-line rail and integrating bus services. The Cardiff Capital Region has invested in electrifying valley rail lines. The metro is operating with rolling upgrades in 2025-2026.

geographicScopeIssue.issue: Page titled and slugged '/south-wales' covers only the south Wales valleys; 'South Wales' is a much broader geography
geographicScopeIssue.detail: The TS data file focuses specifically on the industrial valleys (Rhondda, Cynon, Taff, Rhymney) and Brecon Beacons access. However, 'South Wales' as commonly understood also includes: the Vale of Glamorgan, Cardiff coast, Newport/Monmouthshire, Bridgend/Porthcawl, and parts of Neath Port Talbot. The Gower Peninsula has its own location page (/gower). A user searching Google for 'South Wales adventure activities' will have broader expectations than this valleys-focused page delivers. This creates an SEO scope mismatch.
geographicScopeIssue.action: HUMAN EDITORIAL DECISION: either (1) broaden the /south-wales page to cover the wider south Wales geography (adding Vale of Glamorgan coast, Porthcawl surf, caving in the Brecon Beacons foothills, Newport/Caerleon heritage, etc.); or (2) explicitly frame the page as 'South Wales Valleys' (not generic South Wales) with a disambiguation note pointing to other region pages. The current meta.seoTitle already says 'South Wales Valleys' which partially addresses this — but the route slug /south-wales and the data slug 'south-wales' conflict with that framing.
geographicScopeIssue.note: The markdown guide (content/regions/south-wales.md) already leans into the valleys-specific identity with the subheading 'Get Down & Dirty' and explicitly tells users seeking beaches/coast to go to Gower or Pembrokeshire. This editorial choice should be made consistent across both files.

The markdown guide (content/regions/south-wales.md) explicitly calls out caving as the second-best activity after mountain biking — but the TS data file has no caving entry in topExperiences or bestFor (rank 1-10). This is a significant content gap.
contentGaps.action: Add caving to topExperiences. The National Showcaves Centre for Wales (Dan yr Ogof) is the most accessible caving/cave show attraction: https://www.showcaves.co.uk/. For adventure caving, Porth yr Ogof (NRW managed) is a well-known entry point: https://www.naturalresources.wales/days-out/the-countryside/south-wales/porth-yr-ogof/. Verify current access and guided tour options.

blockers.resolution: HUMAN ACTION: (1) add meta.socialImage: '/images/regions/south-wales-og.jpg' to data/regions/south-wales.ts; (2) source or create a 1200×630px OG image — candidates include Openverse (https://openverse.org/search/?q=mountain+biking+south+Wales&license_type=commercial&use_commercial=true) or Visit Wales media library (https://www.visitwales.com/trade/media-centre); (3) record full provenance (photographer, licence, source URL, attribution) in the image registry before publishing.

blockers.blocker: '30 minutes from Cardiff' keyFact for Merthyr Tydfil/Brecon Beacons access is likely inaccurate, and Cwmcarn Forest operational status unverified
blockers.detail: keyFacts[3] states Cardiff to Merthyr Tydfil/Brecon Beacons is '30 minutes'. Transport for Wales valley line trains take approximately 55-65 minutes. This is a material visitor planning error. Additionally topExperiences[3] lists Cwmcarn Forest Trails as an active trail centre — Cwmcarn Forest Drive had extended closures due to Phytophthora larch disease and the MTB trails have had intermittent access issues. Publishing incorrect journey time and a potentially-closed trail centre will cause visitor frustration and erode trust.
blockers.resolution: For travel time: verify current TfW journey times at https://www.tfwrail.wales/ and correct keyFacts[3].value. For Cwmcarn: verify current MTB trail and Forest Drive operational status with NRW at https://www.naturalresources.wales/days-out/the-countryside/south-east-wales/cwmcarn-forest/ — if trails are closed or restricted, update or remove the topExperiences entry.

blockers.detail: public/images/regions/south-wales-hero.jpg (308KB) exists on disk but has no photographer credit, licence type, or acquisition record in the image registry — publishing it is a copyright risk. Separately, the page has only 5 topExperiences (vs 12 for Pembrokeshire, 10 for most regions) and only 3 FAQs. Caving — which the markdown guide identifies as the second-best activity — is entirely absent from the TS data. The page currently lacks the depth needed to provide genuine value to visitors or rank well in search.
blockers.resolution: For the hero image: audit acquisition records; if provenance cannot be established, source a replacement via Openverse or Visit Wales media library with a verified licence. For content depth: a human content writer should expand topExperiences to 8-12 entries (adding caving, surfing at Porthcawl, Pen y Fan summit walk), expand FAQs to 6-10 questions, and verify Bike Park Wales pricing and T4 bus operation. The fastest path to publishable quality is resolving the image blockers and running a single content expansion pass.
